title: Mobile verified loopback runtime origin
objective: Serve receipt-verified bundled Sage.js runtime assets from an application-owned capability-bearing 127.0.0.1 origin on iOS and Android with strict isolation/security headers and lifecycle cleanup

oracles: Native unit tests and TypeScript contract tests for allowlisting, traversal, headers, lifecycle, and WebView navigation
exceptions: Swift and Kotlin adapters are platform host primitives required to own a loopback TCP origin without broad third-party native dependencies.

runs.command: env ANDROID_HOME=/home/user/Android/Sdk apps/sagejs-mobile/android/gradlew -p apps/sagejs-mobile/android testDebugUnitTest assembleDebug -x verifySageRuntime --no-daemon

handoff.summary: iOS and Android now verify the complete signed mobile/production receipt closure before serving allowlisted assets from an ephemeral 127.0.0.1 port and 256-bit capability path. Both native servers enforce traversal, method, MIME, caching, CSP, COOP/COEP/CORP, no-cookie, lifecycle, and external-bind restrictions; React Native WebView uses only that exact origin and stops it in the background. Android native tests and a full debug APK compile pass.
risks: This Linux host cannot compile the Swift bridge. The Xcode project includes both new source files, but macOS simulator compilation remains required before release.

The debug Android manifest includes React Native developer permissions; the merged release manifest was separately verified to contain only INTERNET plus AndroidX's app-scoped signature permission and no storage permission.
next_steps: Add a macOS GitHub Actions job that prepares the exact attested assets, installs pods, and builds both iPhone and iPad simulator destinations.

Extend the physical-device receipt schema and runtime-ready evidence with URL scheme/host, crossOriginIsolated, SharedArrayBuffer, and outer/nested worker topology, then collect actual iPhone/iPad/TestFlight receipts.
Run the WebKit memory lane's independent loopback-origin worker/isolation probe against this native policy.
